published_prior_art.cite: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional proves local intervention-size necessity/sufficiency and an O(n^2) algorithm, not a bounded-size adaptive finite-versus-infinite minimax count frontier.

VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional gives a headwise O(n^2) CADIM schedule; ShanmugamKocaogluDimakisVishwanath2015SmallInterventions gives single-DAG separating-system constructions, but neither states this mixture parent-blocker cover.

VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional assumes I-mixture faithfulness; generic faithful finite-DAG parameterizations are standard, but the proposed simultaneous shared-intervention realization is a technical bridge rather than a distinct prior frontier.
VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional, Conclusion: constrained-size intervention-count lower bounds remain open; single-DAG count papers assume a known skeleton or essential graph.
GreenewaldKatzShanmugamEtAl2019CausalTrees gives a factor-two adaptive policy for one causal tree, not exact counts for heterogeneous directed-tree mixtures.
VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional, Theorem 3, gives an O(n^2) cycle-free-ancestor recovery algorithm with locally optimal intervention size, not an exact adaptive count law.
No cited paper states these full-oracle mixture counts; they are useful benchmarks and constraints on the main frontier rather than an independently broad literature advance.

soundness_flags.one_line: The model stores only observational component laws, while P_{ell,I}, the shared target mechanisms, their graph-factorization relation, and the defining relation between Delta and mechanism variation are never specified, so the interventional-law and simultaneous-faithful-realization claims are not defined over the declared class.

soundness_flags.one_line: Membership in M_{n,K,d,0} already entails tau(G)<=0 and hence tau(G)=0, making ass:cyclefree-ancestors redundant in the cycle-free subclass.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5-9, Theorems 1-4; p. 9, Conclusion; Appendix B.3, p. 14.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves local worst-case intervention size |pa_m(i)|+1, gives CADIM with O(n^2) interventions, and explicitly identifies constrained-size intervention-count lower bounds as future work.
The paper proves deterministic adaptive learning of complete single-DAG skeletons requires a separating system and studies bounded-size interventions.
The paper studies adaptive experiment design for one causal tree and proves its centrality algorithm uses at most twice the minimum achievable interventions under very large interventional samples.
The paper constructs a graphical representation encoding conditional independences of mixture distributions and studies observational structure learning of component-DAG unions.
The paper characterizes minimal verifying interventions through covered edges and gives bounded-size and cost extensions for single-DAG verification/search.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract, especially the r-adaptive approximation statement.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The actual paper is titled Adaptivity Complexity for Causal Graph Discovery and proves the stated O(min{r,log n} n^(1/min{r,log n})) approximation relative to the verification number for single-DAG discovery.
The paper optimizes interventions when a single-DAG skeleton is given, including limited-intervention algorithms for tree and clique-tree skeletons.

The paper identifies graphical properties under latent population mixtures using ranks of agglomerated moment matrices when latent-class count is small relative to DAG size and sparsity; this is a different information model from complete CI-oracle intervention design.
